title: prompt-library-scratchpad-maya-ross
content:
Purpose:
- Working scratchpad for prompt templates, few-shot sets, and documented failure cases.
- Target: a lightweight prompt library (JSON + short examples) for internal consumption by SDK users and solutions engineers.

Notes to self (quick):
- Keep templates generic but include 2-3 model-specific flavors (gpt-like, open-llama-like, opt/decoder variations).
- Need to track token-cost delta for each template variant (rough per-1000-token cost).
- Prioritize classification/extraction/rewrites and multi-turn instruction scaffolding.

1) Template: classification (binary + multi-class)
- Prompt v1 (concise):
  """You are an assistant that extracts labels. Given the text, respond with one label from: [POSITIVE, NEGATIVE, NEUTRAL]. Provide just the label.
  Text: {input}
  """
- Prompt v2 (robust few-shot):
  """Label the sentiment of the text. Only output one of: POSITIVE | NEGATIVE | NEUTRAL.
  Example 1:
  Text: I love the new UI, it's super fast.
  Label: POSITIVE
  Example 2:
  Text: The update broke my workflow and I lost time.
  Label: NEGATIVE
  Example 3:
  Text: It's okay — sometimes slow but usable.
  Label: NEUTRAL
  Now label the following:
  Text: {input}
  Label:
  """
- Observations: few-shot helps on rare phrasing but increases cost. For Llama-like models, providing 2 examples is often enough. For gpt-like, single example + stronger instruction works.

2) Template: extraction (entities / structured fields)
- Schema-first style (preferred):
  """Extract the following fields from the text. Output JSON with keys exactly: {name, date, invoice_amount}. If a field is missing, use null.
  Text: {input}
  Output:
  """
- Few-shot variant: include 2 sample inputs + outputs.
- Failure modes seen: model paraphrases field names, returns prose, wraps in backticks, or returns additional keys. Mitigation: explicit phrasing "Output JSON with keys exactly: ..." and post-validate on client side.

3) Template: rewrite / tone / summarization
- Short instruction variant for low-cost usage:
  """Rewrite the following into a friendly, concise sentence (<=20 words): {input}\  """
- Few-shot for style control: 2 examples of before/after.
- Notes: when length constraint is strict, add "Do not add information" and include an absolute token ceiling in the client call (max_tokens).

4) Multi-turn scaffolding (system + user + assistant)
- System: "You are Redwood Inference assistant for internal tools. When asked to perform extraction or classification, always return machine-parseable output unless user explicitly asks for prose."
- Use conversation history prefixing: collapse assistant confirmations into short context lines to reduce token usage.

Few-shot sets (candidates):
- Sentiment-set-A (3 examples): good for gpt-class models
- Extraction-set-B (2 examples + edge-cases): includes missing fields, ambiguous dates, multiple currencies
- Rewriting-set-C: shows different tone levels (formal -> casual -> marketing)

Failure cases (observed during ad-hoc tests 2025-11 -> 2026-01):
- Hallucinated numbers: invoice_amount sometimes ~10x unrealistic. Root cause: model invents plausible numbers when date context ambiguous.
  - Example input: "Invoice due: next week. Total: see attached." -> Model returns 3492.12.
  - Mitigation: prefer "If amount not present, return null" and add an explicit constraint: "Do NOT fabricate numbers." Still not perfect.
- Extra keys / prose: models wrapping JSON in text.
  - Mitigation: post-parse heuristics (strip code fences, parse last JSON-looking token, fallback to regex extraction).
- Ambiguous label mapping (NEUTRAL vs NEGATIVE): short prompts can flip on subtle sarcasm.
  - Mitigation: add an example with sarcasm or use calibration set + thresholding if using LM logits (not available in hosted API).
- Truncation / context window issues: for long docs, earlier context lost, causing missed extractions.
  - Mitigation: client-level chunking + rolling extraction. Add instructions: "If important information may appear earlier, ask for up to N preceding sentences."

Evaluation metrics to track (minimal):
- Exact match rate (for JSON extraction), F1 for entity spans, macro-F1 for multi-class classification
- Token cost per successful example (avg tokens in/out * token_price)
- Latency P50/P95 on real workload (important for decision of few-shot vs zero-shot)
- Failure taxonomy counts (hallucination, format violation, truncation)

Experiment plan (short):
- A/B test prompt v1 (concise) vs v2 (few-shot) on 1000 annotated samples
  - Track cost delta, EM, and timeouts
- Model matrix: test on 3 model families: redwood-gpt-small, open-llama-7b, meta-opt-6.7b (or their equivalents)
- Postprocessing ablation: aggressive JSON extraction vs permissive regex fallback

Quick TODOs:
- [ ] Add 10 more sarcasm examples to sentiment few-shot set (priority: high)
- [ ] Build a lightweight JS validator for returned JSON (strip wrappers, ensure keys exist) (owner: Jordan K.)
- [ ] Add token-cost delta table per-template (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Link to canonical Prompt Library spec + update confluence page with sample sets

Open questions / unresolved:
- Do we prefer system-level constraints (system message) or in-prompt constraints for private deployments? (need infra input on enforcement)
- How to version these prompt templates? Suggest simple semver per-template (v1, v1.1) + checksum.

Scratch experiments (notes):
- Tried: "Only return JSON" + 3 examples -> reduced prose but still sometimes wrapped in markdown. Post-strip is necessary.
- Tried: explicit negative instruction: "Do NOT output any explanation" -> models comply mostly but sometimes add a final ":" or whitespace.

References and links:
- Internal: Prompt Library Spec on Confluence (link above)
- Tickets: linear PR-413 for initial design
- Implementation PR: github PR #27 (early JSON schema)

Personal notes: keep this doc light. When stable, port selected templates to /shared_drives/product/console-and-rollouts/prompt-library-examples and create small README for SDK snippets.

-- Maya
